content.text: {"primary_meaning": "In most Christian teaching, leaven symbolizes sin, corruption, or evil influence—especially false teaching and hypocrisy—whose defining characteristic is that a small amount spreads pervasively through the whole. This underlies the moral logic of removing leaven at Passover and the apostolic exhortation to purge sin from the community.", "primary_basis": ["Exodus 12:14-20 (removal of leaven for Passover/Feast of Unleavened Bread)", "Exodus 13:3-7", "Leviticus 2:11 (leaven excluded from grain offerings burned to the LORD)", "Matthew 16:6-12 (leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees, identified as their teaching)", "Mark 8:15 (leaven of the Pharisees and of Herod)", "Luke 12:1 (leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy)", "1 Corinthians 5:6-8 ('a little leaven leavens the whole lump'; purge out the old leaven of malice and evil)", "Galatians 5:9 ('a little leaven leavens the whole lump,' applied to false teaching)"], "alternatives": [{"meaning": "Leaven as a positive image of the hidden, gradual, pervasive growth of the Kingdom of God / the gospel's transforming influence in the world, based on Jesus' parable of the leaven.", "basis": ["Matthew 13:33", "Luke 13:20-21"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "A negative reading of the parable of the leaven itself: leaven in Matthew 13:33 represents evil or false doctrine infiltrating and corrupting professing Christendom, on the argument that leaven is consistently negative elsewhere in Scripture. Associated especially with some dispensationalist and older fundamentalist commentators (e.g., Scofield tradition).", "basis": ["Matthew 13:33 read in light of Leviticus 2:11, Matthew 16:6-12, 1 Corinthians 5:6-8, Galatians 5:9"], "prominence": "minority"}, {"meaning": "Leaven as a neutral, non-symbolic element of ordinary life: it is permitted or even required in certain offerings, suggesting it is not inherently a symbol of evil but simply an image of pervasive influence (good or bad depending on context).", "basis": ["Leviticus 7:13 (leavened bread with the peace/thanksgiving offering)", "Leviticus 23:17 (leavened loaves at Pentecost/Feast of Weeks)", "Amos 4:5"], "prominence": "minority"}, {"meaning": "Leaven as specifically 'hypocrisy'—a narrower application of the negative sense, sometimes treated as its own distinct definition rather than a subset of general corruption.", "basis": ["Luke 12:1"], "prominence": "common"}], "has_settled_consensus": true, "confidence": "high", "notes": "There is a broad, recognizable consensus that leaven in Scripture predominantly symbolizes sin, corruption, hypocrisy, or false doctrine that spreads pervasively, grounded in the Passover regulations and the explicit Pauline and Synoptic usages. The main interpretive dispute concerns the parable of the leaven (Matthew 13:33 / Luke 13:20-21): the majority of commentators across traditions read it positively (kingdom growth), which creates the acknowledged tension that leaven is not uniformly negative; a minority (notably in dispensationalist circles) insists on a consistently negative symbolism and reads the parable as corruption within Christendom. Both the dominant negative meaning and the common positive parable reading are well established in published interpretation."}
